prompt: Which statement correctly defines accuracy according to the Cambridge 9702 syllabus?
options: The degree of agreement among repeated measurements, indicated by their spread or range.
The smallest division marked on the scale of an analogue measuring instrument.
The closeness of a measured value to the true value of the quantity.
The total number of decimal places recorded in a table of experimental data.

answer.explanation: Accuracy is defined as the closeness of a measured value to the true value of the quantity.

distractor_explanations: This defines scale division or resolution.
Correct. Accuracy describes how close a measured value is to the true value.
Decimal places relate to display formatting and resolution, not accuracy.
hints: Accuracy requires comparison with the true value.
Recall the controlled syllabus wording: closeness to the true value.
solution: Accuracy is the closeness of a measured value to the true value of the quantity.
teacher_walkthrough: Accuracy measures proximity to the true or accepted reference value.
Recall the controlled definition: the closeness of a measured value to the true value of the quantity.

provenance.independence_statement: Authored to test verbatim recall of the Cambridge definition of accuracy.
